A parent used Young's formula to calculate the required medication dosage for their child. Young's formula is
$$\text{Dosage} = \frac{\text{Age of child (years)} \times \text{Adult dose}}{\text{Age of child (years)} + 12}.$$
They found that the child's dosage was one quarter of the adult dose. How old is the child?
questions.answer:
Let the age be $a$ and the adult dose $d$:
$$\frac{ad}{a + 12} = \frac{d}{4} \Rightarrow 4a = a + 12 \Rightarrow a = 4$$
The child is **4 years old**.

questions.question:
Ashaal is standing at a lookout. She looks up and sees a seagull. The seagull is 153 m from Ashaal at an angle of elevation of 63°. Ashaal then looks down and sees the seagull's nest directly below the seagull. The nest is 87 m from Ashaal at an angle of depression of 27°.

Draw a labelled diagram to represent this information. Hence, calculate the distance between the seagull and its nest. Give your answer to the nearest metre.
questions.answer:
The angle at Ashaal between the two sight lines is $63^\circ + 27^\circ = 90^\circ$, so the triangle (Ashaal, seagull, nest) is right-angled at Ashaal:
$$d = \sqrt{153^2 + 87^2} \approx 176\text{ m}$$
(The given data is not fully consistent: other valid methods, e.g. the sine rule or vertical heights, give about 192 m, and the school accepted both.)

| Study hours | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mark (%) | 52 | 58 | 61 | 68 | 72 | 77 | 81 | 85 |

A line of best fit for the data is: Mark $= 4.7(\text{Study hours}) + 44$.

A student claims that studying for an extra hour will always increase their examination mark by about 5%. Use the data and the line of best fit to analyse this claim.
questions.answer:
- The gradient of the line of best fit is 4.7, so on average each extra hour is associated with about 4.7 more marks, close to 5.
- The actual data does not rise by the same amount each hour (rises of 6, 3, 7, 4, 5, 4, 4), so it is not "always" 5%.
- The line is a model of the trend; individual results vary around it, and it can't be extended indefinitely (marks are capped at 100%). The claim is only approximately true on average, not always.

Scientists perform two wildlife surveys six months apart to estimate the total koala population in a valley. In the first survey they tagged 70 koalas and then released them back into the wild. In the second survey six months later, they caught and checked 100 koalas. Of these 100 koalas, 35 had tags.

The scientists then discovered that 6 of the koalas that had been tagged in the first survey had been moved to another location to help with a breeding program, so were not in the valley at the time of the second survey. What is the better estimate for the number of koalas in the valley at the time of the second survey?
questions.answer:
Only $70 - 6 = 64$ tagged koalas were in the valley:
$$T = \frac{64 \times 100}{35} \approx 182.9 \approx 183\text{ koalas}$$

Each town is to be connected to a new water supply. By drawing a minimum spanning tree, calculate the minimum length of pipes required to supply water to all towns if the water pipes can only be laid along the roads.
questions.answer:

questions.question:
A large farm shed has a flat rectangular roof which is 12 metres wide by 24 metres long. During a thunder storm 20 mm of rain falls onto the roof in 10 minutes. Rain that falls on the roof drains immediately into a cylindrical rainwater tank with a diameter of 4 metres.

Calculate the average rate at which the water level in the tank changes during the storm. Answer in centimetres per minute to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
Water: $12 \times 24 \times 0.02 = 5.76\text{ m}^3$. The tank's base area is $\pi(2)^2 = 4\pi\text{ m}^2$:
$$h = \frac{5.76}{4\pi} \approx 0.4584\text{ m} = 45.84\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{45.84}{10} \approx 4.6\text{ cm/min}$$

questions.question:
A project requires activities $A$ to $F$ to be completed. The activity chart shows the immediate prerequisites and duration for each activity.

| Activity | Immediate prerequisite(s) | Duration (minutes) |
|---|---|---|
| A | – | 6 |
| B | A | 2 |
| C | A | 4 |
| D | C | 3 |
| E | B, D | 2 |
| F | C | 4 |

A new activity, $X$, is added to the project, and has $A$ as an immediate prerequisite. No other activity has $X$ as an immediate prerequisite.

By first drawing a network diagram showing all seven activities, find the maximum duration of $X$ if it does not increase the minimum time to complete the project.
questions.answer:
Critical path $A$–$C$–$D$–$E$: $6 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 15$ minutes (paths $A$–$B$–$E$ = 10, $A$–$C$–$F$ = 14).

$X$ can start at 6 and must finish by 15:
$$\text{Maximum duration of } X = 15 - 6 = 9\text{ minutes}$$

questions.question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AC = 10$ cm, $AB = 6$ cm and $\angle ACB = 20^\circ 41'$. Given that $\angle ABC$ is obtuse, find the size of $\angle BAC$ to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{\sin\angle ABC}{10} = \frac{\sin 20^\circ 41'}{6} \Rightarrow \angle ABC = 36^\circ 4' \text{ (acute)}$$
It is obtuse, so $\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 36^\circ 4' = 143^\circ 56'$.
$$\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 143^\circ 56' - 20^\circ 41' = 15^\circ 23'$$

Theatre tickets were purchased for a total of \$478 using the credit card. Full payment was made on the 62nd day from the date of purchase. There are no other purchases on this credit card. What was the total interest charged when the account was paid in full?
questions.answer:
Interest runs from day 31 to day 62 inclusive: 32 days.
$$A = 478\left(1 + \frac{0.1299}{365}\right)^{32} \approx \$483.47 \Rightarrow \text{Interest} \approx \$5.47$$

questions.question:
A financial adviser writes the following post:

"If two investments have the same annual interest rate, they will earn exactly the same amount of interest over the same time period. The compounding frequency makes no difference."

To support the claim, the financial adviser shows the following calculations.

| Investment | Principal | Interest rate | Compounding | Time | Final balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | \$10 000 | 6% p.a. | Annually | 5 years | \$13 382.26 |
| B | \$10 000 | 6% p.a. | Monthly | 5 years | \$13 382.26 |

Analyse the financial adviser's claim. In your response: calculate the correct final balance for Investment B; identify any errors in the financial adviser's reasoning; determine whether the claim is valid; justify your conclusion using appropriate calculations and financial reasoning.
questions.answer:
- A: $10\,000(1.06)^5 = \$13\,382.26$ (correct).
- B: $10\,000\left(1 + \frac{0.06}{12}\right)^{60} \approx \$13\,488.50$, not \$13 382.26.

The adviser applied the annual formula to B, ignoring the monthly compounding. B earns \$106.24 more, because interest is added more often and then earns interest itself. **The claim is not valid**: with the same annual rate, more frequent compounding gives a larger final balance.
